proof_summary: Above the cutoffs, positivity supplies a witness whose parity specialization gives respectively \(n=p+q\) or \(n=p+2q\), while finite primality searches establish both representation claims below the cutoffs. For any bound \(x\), applying the hypothesis to \(n=2(x+4007)\) yields \(2q<n\), so the cousin-prime pair \((n-q-6,n-q)\) lies beyond \(x\), proving that such pairs are unbounded and hence infinite.
